            HOW TO make a DLL wrapper using the "wrap_dll"
            ==============================================
            
0. Not yet resolved: 
    0.1 linked dependencies of wrapped DLLs
    0.2 cpp exported classes or methods
    0.3 NOTE: __stdcall stack issue for unresolved links (OpenCL.dll)
    0.4 DLL versioning
    0.5 real wrappers number against declarations verification
    0.6 DLL load/search path
    0.7 DLL load counter and function to get the load count
    0.8 Perhaps, print the name of unresolved fucntion call

1. The "wrap_dll" is implemented by "platform/win32/wrap_dll.cpp" and some macros

2. The wrap_dll.h defines prototypes, macros to be used in wrapper and in callers code

3. The DLL wrapper is (normally) based on:
    3.1 DLL exported functions - to get a list of finctions and decoration
    3.2 the .h file with DLL interface declaration
    
4. Application caller code should be modified:
    4.1 add *one* wrap_XXXXX_Init function (to load and wrap the DLL)
    4.2 [optionaly, if needed] add one wrap_XXXXX_Term function

5. Each DLL wrapper, normally placed on wrap_XXXXX.cpp should have following parts:
    5.1 Wrapper name (just C-like identifier), will be used in many places
          #define WRAPPER_NAME        the_good_C_like_name      
          
    5.2 Pragma "lib" and faked implementation of Init/Term functions for the linked form of use.
        Example:
            #pragma comment( lib, "OpenCL.lib" )
            
            UINT32 wrap_OpenCL_Init ( void )
            {
                return( WRAP_DLL_LINKED( WRAPPER_NAME ) );         // just give a printout
            }//wrap_OpenCL_init
            UINT32 wrap_OpenCL_Term ( void )
            {
                return( UNWRAP_DLL_LINKED( WRAPPER_NAME ) );         // just give a printout
            }//wrap_OpenCL_Term

    5.3 substitution of linkage (ritual dance part 1) __cdecl, __stdcall and  __fastcall) by naked 
        Note, we use __naked functions in wrapper for the performance matter.
        In this form of wrappers every DLL-function call will be surcharged by only
        one instruction
            JMP [dll_function_address]
            
        Example:
            #define  MYDLL_API         __declspec(naked)
    
    5.4 Wrapper declaration begin record(wrapper ritual dance part 2), which has:
        5.4.1 Wrapper data section declaraion and an association of the wrapper with a DLL-filename to load.
            Note: it has to be BEFORE ANY function wrappers
            Example:
                #pragma section(".wrap_info",read,write)
                DECL_WRAPPER_DLL( WRAPPER_NAME, "my-dll-name.dll" );

        5.4.2 A list of functions wrappers (implementations).
            This list is normally done using a copy of the .H of the DLL.
            Just take the function declaration from the H-file and
            add the implemenation body as WRAP_CALL2JUMP( function_name )
            Note, the function name is used *twice*, as a function name AND
                as a parameter of macro WRAP_CALL2JUMP.
                
            Example:
                PS3EYEMULTICAM_API bool STATIC_MAAAPIENTRY_PS3	
                PS3EyeMulticamSaveSettings( char* fileName /*="settings.xml"*/ )
                    WRAP_CALL2JUMP( PS3EyeMulticamSaveSettings );
    
        
        5.4.3 wrapper closing record (wrapper ritual dance part 3) and
            implementation of the wrap_dll-infrastaructure functions
            NOTE: this part has to be placed AFTER ALL function wrappers

            Example:
                DECL_WRAPPER_END( WRAPPER_NAME );
    
            5.4.3.1 wrap_XXXXX_Init(void) - DLL loader and  wrappers linker for the DLL function
                Macro to use in the body: WRAP_DLL( WRAPPER_NAME ). 
            Example:
            UINT32  wrap_censys_Init ( void )
            {
                return( WRAP_DLL( WRAPPER_NAME ) );
            }
    
            5.4.3.2 wrap_XXXXX_Term(void) - unload the DLL and relink functions to UNDEFINED
                Macro to use in the body: UNWRAP_DLL( WRAPPER_NAME ). 
            Example:
                UINT32  wrap_censys_Init ( void )
                {
                    return( WRAP_DLL( WRAPPER_NAME ) );
                }
    
            5.4.3.3 static _unresolved_call() - this function will be called for every
                unresolved call for the wrapped DLL (if any).   
                Macro to use in the body: WRAP_UNRESOLVED( WRAPPER_NAME ).
                Note, the return code (int) has to have a DLL-meaning.
            Example:
                int     //CENSYS_ERROR 
                _unresolved_call ( void )
                {
                    WRAP_UNRESOLVED( WRAPPER_NAME );
                return( (int) censyserrorSYSTEM_INIT_ERROR );
                }
            
6. General note on the __stdcall/__cdecl exported functions:
    Functions declared as __stdcall balance their stack by callee.
    This make the stack frame (parameters size) unknown in the wrapper.
    (Note, remember our wrapers are __naked for the efficiency reason)
    So, any "unresolved" call to such (__stdcall) a function will crash the
    application, with an error message and the DLL name, however, as a "last adieu".
    The information about function name is not available (in this implementation)
    
7. More real examples:
    Search for the wrap_*.cpp and wrap_*.h files in AAASeed sources.
    (wrap_censys, wrap_isence etc.)

8. In order to be sure, everything is good generated - cearch the mapfile for
    _w_beg_* and _w_end_* globals. All _p_* and _n_* wrappers have to be placed in between.
    All wrappers data is placed into the ".wrap_info" segment(section).

=== end ===
